//: Known Chrome/Edge incompatibilities that exist today. tests/compat.test.mjs fails on any violation NOT listed here, and also fails on any entry here that no longer matches — so this file cannot drift from reality. Milestone 2 deletes entries as it ports each area. Keys are '<file>::<ruleId>'.

background.js::sidebarAction.reason: background.js:114 calls sidebarAction.toggle(). Chrome has sidePanel.open() with no toggle, and loses gesture context across the preceding await.

background.js::menus-namespace.reason: Ported. The single remaining reference is the feature-detect `browser.menus || browser.contextMenus`; every call site now goes through that alias, so Chrome uses contextMenus.

background.js::menus-onShown-refresh.reason: Ported. onShown/refresh are now inside a capability branch used only on Firefox, where they're the cheapest correct option. Chrome takes the else-branch: eager syncToggleCheckmarks() driven by storage.onChanged, plus a resync when a toggle's sendMessage fails.

background.js::getSecurityInfo.reason: Ported. Guarded by CAN_READ_TLS (a typeof check on the function itself), so it only runs on Firefox. Chrome leaves entry.tls unset and popup-dns.js falls back to #tls-note. The call has to stay in the source — this is the Firefox branch.

background.js::webRequest-blocking.reason: Ported. The ['blocking','responseHeaders'] literal is now the Firefox arm of HEADERS_SPEC, selected by the same CAN_READ_TLS check — 'blocking' existed solely to make getSecurityInfo work. Chrome registers with ['responseHeaders'] only.

background.js::originUrl.reason: Ported. Now reads `d.originUrl || d.initiator`, accepting Firefox's property or Chrome's. The Firefox name necessarily remains in the source.

background.js::moz-extension-scheme.reason: Ported. The self-request check accepts moz-extension:// or chrome-extension://. The Firefox scheme necessarily remains in the source.

popup.js::getViews-sidebar.reason: popup.js:7 detects sidebar mode via extension.getViews({type:'sidebar'}), which is Firefox-only and returns [] on Chrome — silently disabling the follow-active-tab block. Replace with the ?view=sidepanel marker the chrome manifest already sets.

popup-redirects.js::onMessage-promise-re.reason: False positive. popup-redirects.js:377 is a fire-and-forget listener for the redirectUpdated broadcast — it never needs to reply, so having no sendResponse is correct on both browsers.
